• Before you get started, please ensure that you have an active, paid Azure subscription.
    • {br}
  • You need to generate a tenant URL and an authentication token for your clients in SuperOps and map them to the respective clients in Azure. Once the clients are mapped, the client’s data in Azure will be synced with SuperOps.

admin.integrations.bitdefender.commonDes: Defend your organization's networks from a multitude of online threats by integrating Bitdefender with SuperOps. admin.integrations.bitdefender.config.st: Before you get started, please ensure that you have a paid, active Bitdefender subscription. Log in to your Bitdefender account to obtain the necessary pieces of information to connect your Bitdefender account with SuperOps.

Once you're logged in to Bitdefender, the first thing you'll need is the API access URL. This access URL helps the platform identify which region your account is from. You can find this in the My Account section, under Control Center API.

The second thing you'll need is the API key. This API key authenticates the connection between both tools, and helps us retrieve package information about the devices in your network. You can find the API key in the Control Center API section as well.

Please ensure that the API key provided has access to the following modules in Bitdefender: Packages, Network, and Companies. Once you've filled in both fields below, click connect to complete the connection process and start syncing your databases.

admin.integrations.connectwise.descripti: Integrate SuperOps with ConnectWise Control to run remote access sessions to diagnose issues in your client's endpoints and fix them in no time.
admin.integrations.connectwise.instructi:
• Please ensure that you have an active, paid ConnectWise Control subscription.
    • {br}
  • Install the ConnectWise Control agents generated from your ConnectWise Control account on your clients' assets.
    • {br}
  • Provide the ConnectWise Control URL—this URL is unique and is mapped to your company's name, similar to the subdomain you have in SuperOps.
    • {br}
  • Next, you'll need to provide the instance ID for ConnectWise Control. Here's how you can find it:
    • {br}
    • Install the agent in your device.
      • {br}
    • Load up the task manager, where you'll find the instance ID within parentheses after ConnectWise Client. For example, it'll look like ConnectWise Client (fd39834nbc)
      • {br}
    • Please ensure that the Connectwise Instance ID provided matches the Instance ID of your assets. The integration won't go through if there is any mismatch.
    {br}
  • Fill in the name of the session group you want to group your remote access sessions under in ConnectWise Control and click Save.

admin.integrations.pax8.enable.descripti:
You’re just one click away from activating Pax8 for SuperOps!{br}{br}Some nuggets of wisdom before you get started:{br}
  • Once Pax8 is enabled, we’ll add all existing Pax8 subscriptions to their corresponding client contracts in SuperOps.
    • {br}
  • Haven’t created a contract for a client yet? Not a problem. We’ll create one automatically with all their subscriptions from Pax8. (You’ll still need to start the contract and set up an invoicing schedule though, don’t forget!)
    • {br}
  • A neat way SuperOps helps manage client subscriptions: The platform scans for updates once every 24 hours—when new subscriptions are added in Pax8, they’ll automatically be added to the corresponding mapped clients in SuperOps. You can also choose to manually sync them in the contracts session for the client in SuperOps.
    • {br}
  • Your clients need to be mapped between both platforms for us to bring in their subscription info. If a new client is added, then they’ll need to be mapped in Step 2, after which we’ll start pulling in their subscriptions from Pax8.
{br}{br}Click the button below and you’re off!

admin.integrations.webroot.instructions:
• Before getting started, please ensure that you have an active, paid Webroot account.
    • {br}
  • In your Webroot account, create a Webroot API client. (You can do so in the settings page, in the API access section.) This API client will be useful for connecting Webroot with SuperOps and accessing Webroot through API calls.
    • {br}
  • Make sure that you've added yourself as a super admin in Webroot. If not, then add yourself as a super admin user in Webroot, and set up your login credentials. Keep your email ID and password handy because the super admin's credentials will be used for all API calls.
    • {br}
  • Once you're done setting up the API client and user ID, provide the following information below to connect your Webroot account:
    • {br}
    • GSM key: The global site manager key for your Webroot account
      • {br}
    • Client ID: The client ID you created for API access
      • {br}
    • Client secret: The secret key to authenticate the above client ID, that's provided by Webroot
      • {br}
    • Username: The email ID of the super admin's Webroot account
      • {br}
    • Password: The password for the super admin's Webroot account
    {br}
  • Note: We highly recommend that the above created API client and user credentials only with SuperOps.
Please connect your Webroot account to access this page.

integrations.isl.wfh.instructions:
• Enable, add and save WFH for relevant requesters and client admin of each client.
    • {br}
  • Go to Settings > Roles and groups - Requester roles. Give “view” permission for Assets to your client admins or requesters. Similarly, enable “Remote desktop” for them to take remote sessions.
    • {br}
  • Billing cycle starts on the first day of the month and ends on the last day of the month.
    • {br}
  • Your invoice for the current month will be generated on the 5th of the following month.
    • {br}
  • Adding a new requester, even on the last day of your billing cycle, will be included in your current invoice.
    • {br}
  • Removing a requester during the current billing cycle will only impact the pricing on your next invoice.
    • {br}
  • Requesters or client admins must install the ISL online on their workstation to watch their remote session. You can download the ISL Light viewer app
    • {br}
  • For each user {splashWFHCurrAmount} will be billable
    • {br}
integrations.pax8.activate.desc:

itsm.marketplace.connectwise.instruction:
• Please ensure that you have an active, paid ConnectWise Control subscription.
    • {br}
  • Install the ConnectWise Control agents generated from your ConnectWise Control account on your user's assets.
    • {br}
  • Provide the ConnectWise Control URL—this URL is unique and is mapped to your company's name, similar to the subdomain you have in SuperOps.
    • {br}
  • Next, you'll need to provide the instance ID for ConnectWise Control. Here's how you can find it:
    • {br}
    • Install the agent in your device.
      • {br}
    • Load up the task manager, where you'll find the instance ID within parentheses after ConnectWise Client. For example, it'll look like ConnectWise Client (fd39834nbc)
      • {br}
    • Please ensure that the Connectwise Instance ID provided matches the Instance ID of your assets. The integration won't go through if there is any mismatch.
    {br}
  • Fill in the name of the session group you want to group your remote access sessions under in ConnectWise Control and click Save.

msp.contract.userGuide.oneTime.applicati:
Contract application

Define which contract should be auto-applied to a project from the list of contracts when delivering services.

You can match projects based on conditions or the projects' associations with groups defined in the delivery map, such as projects with all requesters, projects associated with Windows workstation etc.You can choose to auto-approve labor for those services for which the worklogs need not be audited and can skip the audit workflow.

Invoicing

You can choose to send services included in the contract along with other items such as subscriptions, usage-based products, etc., to the billing queue, where you can invoice them together or separately.Invoice directly will generate an invoice instantaneously only for this item, skipping the billing queue.

Ticket Rule Conditions

When a ticket is created, SuperOps checks for contracts that meet the following conditions:

  • The contract's start date is on or before the current date.
  • The contract isn't expired.
  • For site-based contracts, the ticket must be tied to the same site.
  • Draft contracts can still be considered for association.

Once eligible contracts are identified, SuperOps links the one with the highest precedence:

Order of Precedence:

  1. Recurring Contracts
  2. Time and Material Contracts

If there are multiple contracts in the same category, the order from the contracts page is used—you can reorder them anytime.

Contract Activation Triggers

If a draft contract is linked and SLA rules, blacklisted items, or similar features are used, the contract moves to Active automatically. Adding a worklog tied to an included item in the contract also activates it.

Block Hour & Block Money Contracts – Special Rules

  • Must be in Active state to apply.
  • Hours or money are blocked only after the contract is billed.
  • Worklogs won't redeem time or money unless billing has occurred.
msp.contract.userGuide.oneTime.new:
What is this contract for?

Designed for project-based work, these contracts outline a clear scope with a defined start and end date. They're a great fit for one-off tasks that don't require recurring engagement.

💰 Understanding Billing Details

When you're setting up a contract, it's important to get the billing details right—this is what determines how your customer gets charged. Let's break it down:

Pricing Model

You've got two options here:

Fixed Pricing:

You set a predefined total price for the contract. Simple and predictable.

Variable Pricing:

The price is calculated based on actual usage (like number of assets or requests).

Quantity Type

This defines what you're billing for:

Fixed Quantity:

You manually set the number of items to bill. Great for static setups.

Dynamic Quantity:

The quantity adjusts automatically based on groups like Clients, Sites, Assets, or Requesters mapped in the delivery map.
msp.contract.userGuide.package:
What is a package?

A package is a bundle of products and services. You can offer packages as service to clients through contracts. Packages are of two types:

Custom Plans/Tiers

You can bundle products and services and offer them as plans, such as gold plan, platinum plan, etc., each priced differently.

Retainers

Retainers comprise block hours and block money that the client purchases in advance. Once configured, these retainers can be provided through contracts.
msp.contract.userGuide.package.new:
What is a Package?

Packages are bundled offerings that combine multiple services or products into a single plan. You can offer packages through contracts. Packages are of two types:

Custom Plans:

You can bundle products and services and offer them as plans, such as gold plan, platinum plan, etc., each priced differently.

Retainers:

Retainers are prepaid service plans that provide flexibility and predictable billing. There are two types of retainers:

Block Hours:

Clients prepay for a fixed number of support hours (e.g., 10 hours for $500). Additional hours are billed at standard rates.

Block Money:

Clients prepay a fixed amount (e.g., $2000). Charges for services or products are deducted until the prepaid balance is exhausted.
msp.contract.userGuide.product:
What is a product?

A product is an item you provide to your clients. Products can also be provided as a service through contracts (eg: hardware-as-a-service). Product are of two types:

Inventory Items

These are products you keep stock of, such as laptops, SSD, etc.

Non-inventory Items

These are products you provide to clients but do not keep stock of or track, such as software licences.
msp.contract.userGuide.product.new:
What is a Product?

Products are physical or digital items you provide. They can also be provided as service items through contracts. These come in two categories:

Inventory items:

Items you stock and manage fall into this category. For example, Laptops or Monitors.

Non-inventory items:

Items that you don’t maintain stock for but still provide to clients fall into this category. For example, Software licenses.

Hourly Items

Quantity-Based Services:

Hours-Based Services:

product.onboarding.task.contracts.conten:
Know exactly what it costs to deliver your services—not just what you bill for. With delivery maps and automatic time tracking, you get a clear picture of profitability without the extra effort. Here’s what you can do:
  • Choose from 4 contract types for any billing model
  • Bundle services and define granular delivery terms
  • Track revenue, costs, and profitability in real time
  • Bulk update prices across clients in a few clicks
product.onboarding.task.contracts.descri: Build contracts that work the way you do—flexible, clear, and built for profitability.
product.onboarding.task.contracts.title: Learn about contracts
product.onboarding.task.createClientAndD: See how easy it is to add your first client into SuperOps. Try deploying an agent too, while you're at it!
Create your first client and deploy the SuperOps agent
product.onboarding.task.createTemplate.c: Try creating your first template for the most common ticket you get, that one task you do every day, or a frequent project in your pipeline.
product.onboarding.task.createTemplate.d: Don't reinvent the wheel. Invent a template and use it instead.
product.onboarding.task.deliverymap.cont:
No more guesswork or gaps—visualize exactly what’s being delivered, to whom, and how it ties back to your contracts. Here’s what you can do:
  • Set up condition-based groups for users, assets, and sites
  • Map services to each group for precise delivery tracking
  • Align billing and service delivery for better accuracy
  • Give your techs and billing teams shared visibility
product.onboarding.task.deliverymap.desc: Get full clarity on how your services are delivered across users, assets, and sites.
product.onboarding.task.domainEmailConfi: Your domain, your rules—get your support and sales mailboxes up and running in to time.
product.onboarding.task.eventTriggers.co:
The best type of automation is one that quietly removes grunt work off your plate and lets you focus on your work. Event triggers is powerful rule-based automation that lets you do just that—Set once and forget. Here's what you can do:
  • Update ticket properties in response to events
  • Auto-dispatch tickets to technicians/technician groups
  • Assign runbooks and more with advanced automation
product.onboarding.task.eventTriggers.de: Let us do the heavy lifting for you. See how you can leverage powerful workflow automation to get work done faster.
product.onboarding.task.inviteYourTeam.d: Let's get your crew on board! Add your team members here to invite them into the platform.
product.onboarding.task.invoiceAudit.con:
It's important to have complete visibility into what is being added to your client's invoices. The invoice audit gives you a bird's eye view of all line items your team's added across your clients. Skim through, take a call, approve/Reject. That's all there is to it.
  • All products and worklogs from tickets/projects line up here
  • Approval sends it straight to the billing queue for invoicing
  • Modify pricing and add discounts on the go
product.onboarding.task.invoiceAudit.des: See what items your technicians are billing clients for, and decide whether the items make it to the invoice.
product.onboarding.task.invoiceSetting.d: Schedules, settings, and templates—configuration related to your quotes and invoices go here.
product.onboarding.task.manageFields.con:
Be it a default field or a uniquely custom field, take control of your field settings, and configure mandatory info and visibility across your tickets, clients, and requesters.
  • Default and custom fields are neatly arranged across tabs
  • Fields can be made mandatory while creation or closure
  • Set field visibility for clients with a toggle
product.onboarding.task.manageFields.des: Choose what information you'd like to collect for your tickets, clients, and requesters.
product.onboarding.task.manageNotificati: All client-related notifications are right over here.
Be it your clients or your technicians, keep everyone in the loop.
Account activation emails and more for your technicians and requesters go from here.
All ticket notifications for your technicians and requesters are over here.
product.onboarding.task.manageSecurity.d: Safety comes first. Choose the level of protection for your platform to keep your data secure.
product.onboarding.task.networkMonitorin:
Understanding your network's health is crucial for preventing issues and maintaining smooth operations. With network monitoring, monitor your network devices in real-time, receive instant alerts, and keep every asset running smoothly.
  • Deploy probes and start monitoring your network in minutes
  • Schedule network scans to discover new devices on your network
  • Automate asset onboarding with SuperOps’ vast device library
  • Track granular metrics you care about with custom monitors
Learn how you can gain complete network visibility with unified network monitoring.
product.onboarding.task.profitability.co:
With accurate cost inputs and technician time auto-mapped to contracts, your profitability reports are always on point. Here’s what you can do:
  • View MRR, ARR, and contract-level revenue metrics
  • Calculate costs with technician burden rates and service delivery
  • Break down labor revenue by technician and service
  • Identify high- and low-efficiency clients with actionable insights
product.onboarding.task.profitability.de: See how profitable your clients really are—with zero spreadsheets involved.

  • Standardized process-based reply templates
  • Detailed list of tasks to be completed
  • Predefined flow for easy approvals

product.onboarding.task.scheduleAndDispa:
Technicians can schedule events, and Dispatchers can View and Assign events to technicians on the team calendar based on their ticket SLAs for effective resource management.
  • Eliminate conflicts and ensure smooth coordination across teams.
  • Ensure SLAs are not breached with full visibility on technician workloads.
  • Identify the perfect fit for each task with a quick glance at team member icons.
Schedule events and view team calendars for dispatching with 2-way calendar integration

product.onboarding.task.serviceCatalog.c:
The service catalog is Square 1 of your invoicing process. Whether it's a product or a retainer fee, the services you provide have a home in the service catalog. Add them on your own, or import them from bookkeeping tools like QuickBooks or Xero.With SuperOps's invoicing:
  • The grunt work is automated
  • Contract items influence an invoice without intervention
  • Your quotes are converted into invoices in a single click
product.onboarding.task.serviceCatalog.d: Understand how an item from your catalog makes it way to an invoice.

product.onboarding.task.smartTracker.con:
Technicians can accurately track time from anywhere, whether they’re on site or on another website, courtesy mobile and browser extensions. Managers and MSP owners can use technician and client time efficiency insights to optimize resource allocation in real-time and improve client profitability.
  • Track time and analyze tasks
  • Manage and optimize technician times in real-time
  • Strategize better with insights on technician and client efficiencies
product.onboarding.task.smartTracker.des: Track time from anywhere, whether you're on-site on another website. Optimize technician and client efficiency and improve profits.
product.onboarding.task.softWareBundle.c:
Curate software bundles with all the software available through Chocolatey for each client persona and deploy them automatically on your client's devices with ease. With software management:
  • Bundles are deployed on schedule
  • Software updates are handled
  • Removing software is just as easy
product.onboarding.task.softWareBundle.d: Create unique software bundles and deploy them on your client's assets automatically without breaking a sweat.

reports.widget.config.denominator.filter:
• This method calculates the percentage of the group across all available records that meet the filter.
  • It’s helpful for getting an overall picture of the filtered condition, providing a global distribution view.
  • Example: By filtering for paid invoices and grouping the data by client, this method calculates the percentage of each client's total invoices that have been paid. This provides a holistic view of each client's contribution to the overall paid invoice volume.
• This method calculates the percentage of the filter condition based on the group individually.
  • It’s useful when you want to analyze data on a smaller, segmented scale at each group (could be client, site or any field).
  • Example: By grouping invoices by client, this method calculates the percentage of paid invoices for each client individually. This allows you to assess each client's payment performance independently.

splashtop.sos.connect.instruction.mobile:
- Before you get started, ensure that the Splashtop SOS application is installed on the device you want to access remotely.

- Install the 'Splashtop for RMM' app on your mobile to initiate a remote session.

- The registered requester will receive a 9-digit code within the SOS application. Please ask the requester to share this code with you.

- In the provided field above, enter the 9-digit code without using any space or special characters like hyphens.

- Once you've entered the code correctly, simply click the "Connect" button to establish the remote connection.
splashtop.sos.description: Splashtop SOS is an on-demand remote support solution designed for help desk and support professionals. Instantly connect to your users' devices using a simple session code. Combined with SuperOps, initiate ad-hoc remote sessions with ease and keep customers happy.
splashtop.sos.empty.info: Note:{br} New technicians will not receive Splashtop licenses automatically. Admins must add them manually.
splashtop.sos.instructions:
• Enable, add and save SOS for relevant technicians and MSP admins.
    • {br}
  • Go to Settings > Roles and groups - Technician roles. Give “view” permission for Assets to your MSP admins or technicians. Similarly, enable “Remote Desktop” for them to take remote sessions.
    • {br}
  • Billing cycle starts on the first day of the month and ends on the last day of the month.
    • {br}
  • Your invoice for the current month will be generated on the 5th of the following month.
    • {br}
  • Adding a new technician, even on the last day of your billing cycle, will be included in your current invoice.
    • {br}
  • Removing a technician during the current billing cycle will only impact the pricing on your next invoice.
    • {br}
  • Technicians or MSP admins must install the Splashtop Viewer app on their workstation to take a remote session. You can access the Splashtop Viewer app for Windows here. For Mac users, the Splashtop Viewer app can be downloaded here.
    • {br}
  • Download the Splashtop SOS application in the device you want to remote into.
    • {br}
  • For each user {splashWFHCurrAmount} will be billable
    • {br}

admin.employee.empInfo.burdenRate.superp:
What is Burden Rate?

Technician burden rate represents the cost of employing a technician to your MSP, and includes the technician's hourly rate, benefits, and other costs.


  Technician burden rate constitutes a major chunk of your MSP's cost and so is crucial to MSP profitability calculations.


How to calculate

For accurate profitability calculations, please include salary, taxes, insurance, and benefits while determining burn rate.
